ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: As can be seen from the attached figure, the figure is composed of three identical squares: the two squares below are adjacent left and right, sharing a vertical side; the upper square is located directly above this shared vertical side and centered. There is a diagonal line in the figure, from the upper-left corner of the upper square to the lower-right corner of the lower-right square. The gray region includes the part to the right of the diagonal line in the upper square, as well as the triangular part above the right side of the diagonal line in the lower-right square. Reasoning: Let the side length of each square be 1. Place them by coordinates: the lower-left square is [0,1]×[0,1], the lower-right square is [1,2]×[0,1], and the upper square is [1/2,3/2]×[1,2]. The diagonal line passes through the upper-left corner (1/2,2) of the upper square and the lower-right corner (2,0) of the lower-right square. This line intersects the boundary line between the upper and lower squares at y=1. Calculating from the slope, when the line descends from y=2 to y=1, it moves horizontally by 3/4, so the intersection point is x=1/2+3/4=5/4. The unshaded part in the upper square is a right triangle, whose two perpendicular sides are respectively 1 and 3/4, with area (1/2)·1·(3/4)=3/8, so the gray area of the upper square is 1-3/8=5/8. The gray part in the lower-right square is also a right triangle, whose two perpendicular sides are respectively 1 and 3/4, with area 3/8. The total gray area is 5/8+3/8=1.

From the image, observe that the grey area consists of most of the top square plus a triangular grey piece in the lower-right square, while a triangular white piece is cut out of the top square by the same diagonal. Let P be where the diagonal crosses the horizontal line between the top square and the lower squares. They cancel in area, leaving exactly the area of one full unit square, which is 1.
